title: Global algebra and connected components of a proper algebraic space over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum] whose structure map is proper [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Give $|X|$ its atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and let $C$ be its set of connected components, namely maximal nonempty connected subsets. Write $A=\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_X)$ for the ring of global sections of the small etale structure sheaf. Then $C$ is finite, each component is open and closed and hence has its open-subspace structure [def-a1-space-open-subspace], and restriction gives an isomorphism of $k$-algebras
$$A\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{c\in C}\Gamma(c_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_c).$$
The algebra $A$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, and each displayed factor is a nonzero local Artinian $k$-algebra. Here local means having a unique maximal ideal and Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize. If $X$ is reduced (all affine etale chart rings have no nonzero nilpotents), each factor is a finite field extension of $k$. If additionally $k$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], the homomorphism $k^C\to A$ sending $(a_c)$ to the section with constant value $a_c$ on $c$ is an isomorphism; consequently $\dim_k A=\#C$. The empty space is allowed: $C=\varnothing$, $A=0$, and the product is the empty product, the zero ring.

proof.text: Apply the graded-cohomology finiteness theorem with base ring $k$, graded algebra $B=k$ concentrated in degree zero, and $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_X$ concentrated in degree zero. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$; $k$ is finite type over itself with no generators. Its pulled-back algebra is $\mathcal O_X$, and this module is quasi-coherent by the presentation $0\to\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_X\to0$ and is generated by $1$. Thus all the hypotheses of that theorem hold. Its $q=0$ conclusion says that $A$ is a finite $k$-module, since $H^0=\Gamma$ canonically. Hence $A$ is finite-dimensional. The finite-dimensional-algebra lemma makes $A$ Artinian. If $X$ is empty then the sheaf axiom gives $A=0$, and all the assertions follow with empty index set; suppose henceforth that $X$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 0DMY, proof (1), coherent finiteness; use the existing stronger graded form Tag 08AT in degree zero instead of creating an 08AS specialization.

proof.text: Choose a ring decomposition $\phi:A\simeq\prod_{i\in I}B_i$ by the Artinian product theorem, with $I$ finite and each $B_i$ nonzero Artinian local. Give $B_i$ its $k$-algebra structure by the composite $k\to A\xrightarrow{\phi}\prod B_i\to B_i$, so that $\phi$ is a $k$-algebra isomorphism. Let $e_i=\phi^{-1}(\delta_i)$, where $\delta_i$ has entry $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. These are nonzero orthogonal idempotents with $\sum_i e_i=1$. The global-idempotent correspondence supplies clopen subspaces $X_i=U_{e_i}$. They are nonempty because $U_0$ alone corresponds to $0$, and disjoint since $U_{e_i}\cap U_{e_j}=U_0$ for $i\ne j$. They cover $X$: on every affine etale chart the principal opens $D(e_i)$ cover, since their sum is $1$. Thus this is a finite clopen partition.

source.place: Tag 0DMY, proof (2), Artinian decomposition and global idempotents.

proof.text: Restriction gives the asserted product on this partition, with its actual maps. Given sections $s_i$ on the $X_i$, pull them back on any etale scheme test $T\to X$. The opens $T_i=T\times_X X_i$ are disjoint and cover $T$, so the structure-sheaf axiom glues the $s_i|_{T_i}$ to a unique section on $T$. Uniqueness makes these sections compatible with every map of tests. They therefore give a global section on $X$. This construction is inverse to restriction and respects addition, multiplication and constants. Extending a section on $X_i$ by zero on the other opens identifies $\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal O_{X_i})$ with $e_iA$ (identity element $e_i$). Under $\phi$, this is $B_i$. In particular each such section algebra is nonzero local Artinian and finite-dimensional over $k$, as a direct summand of the finite-dimensional algebra $A$.

source.place: Tag 0DMY, proof (2), explicit restriction/gluing interpretation of the product factors.

proof.text:
Each $|X_i|$, with the subspace topology of $|X|$, is connected. Otherwise $|X_i|=W\sqcup W'$ with $W,W'$ nonempty and open in $|X_i|$. Since $|X_i|$ is open and closed in $|X|$, so are $W$ and $W'$. Apply the global-idempotent correspondence to $X$ itself: $W$ is the point image of $U_f$ for an idempotent $f\in A$. Then $U_{fe_i}=U_f\cap U_{e_i}=U_f$, so $fe_i=f$ by the bijection, and $f\in e_iA$; also $f

e|X_i|$. Thus $f$ is an idempotent of $e_iA\simeq\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal O_{X_i})\simeq B_i$ (step 3; identity element $e_i$) different from $0$ and $1$, contradicting the local-ring idempotent lemma. Every connected subset of $|X|$ meets at most one $|X_i|$, because intersection with $|X_i|$ and its complement would otherwise disconnect it. Since each $|X_i|$ is itself nonempty connected and the $|X_i|$ cover $|X|$, these sets are exactly the maximal nonempty connected subsets. Reindex the restriction product of step 3 by $C$. This proves finiteness and openness/closedness of the components and the claimed local Artinian factors.

source.place: Tag 0DMY, proof (2), primitive idempotents identify connected components; this uses the finite partition directly and does not require a separate Noetherian-topology argument.

proof.text: Assume $X$ is reduced. A nilpotent global section restricts to zero on every affine etale chart, because the chart rings are reduced by hypothesis. Restrictions determine a global section, so it is zero. The same argument applies to $X_i$, whose affine etale charts are also charts of $X$. Thus each $B_i$ is reduced. Apply the reduced-Artinian residue-product theorem to $B_i$. Its maximal-ideal set is a singleton since $B_i$ is local, so the canonical product of residue fields is a single field. Consequently $B_i$ is a field. It is finite-dimensional over $k$ by step 3, hence a finite field extension. This proves the reduced clause without any geometric-reducedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0DMY, proof (3); the chartwise reducedness argument also appears in spaces-properties.tex Tag 0BGS.

proof.text: If in addition $k$ is algebraically closed, apply the finite-reduced-algebra-without-idempotents lemma to each $B_i$: it is finite-dimensional by step 3, reduced by step 5, nonzero, and has no nontrivial idempotents by the local-ring lemma. It follows that the structure map $k\to B_i$ is bijective. Taking the finite product and composing with the inverse restriction isomorphism gives $k^C\simeq A$. On the $c$th component it is precisely the structure map $k\to\Gamma(c,\mathcal O_c)$, so it is the homomorphism in the statement, with no choice of field identifications.

source.place: Tag 0DMY, algebraically closed specialization of proof (3), as used in spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0E1E; not clause (7) of 0DMY.

proof.text: The coordinate functions $\delta_c$ in $k^C$ form a basis: every tuple $(a_c)$ is uniquely $\sum_{c\in C}a_c\delta_c$, and evaluating at $c$ shows that a zero sum has all coefficients zero. Transporting this basis through the isomorphism of step 6 gives $\dim_kA=\#C$. For $C=\varnothing$ this is the empty basis of the zero vector space.

lean.statement: theorem proper_global_algebra_components (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (p : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))))) (hp : MapIsProper p) (A : CommAlgCat.{u} k) (π : (Functor.const X.EtaleSiteᵒᵖ).obj (CommRingCat.of A) ⟶ X.etaleForget.op ⋙ Scheme.Γ) (hA : IsLimit (Cone.mk (CommRingCat.of A) π)) (hscalar : ∀ (a : k) (T : X.EtaleSite), (π.app (op T)).hom (algebraMap k A a) = ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ Scheme.Γ.map T.obj.left.hom.op).hom a) : Finite (ConnectedComponents (Point X.obj.obj)) ∧ (∀ c : ConnectedComponents (Point X.obj.obj), IsClopen (ConnectedComponents.mk ⁻¹' {c})) ∧ Module.Finite k A ∧ (IsEmpty (Point X.obj.obj) → Subsingleton A) ∧ ∃ (U : ConnectedComponents (Point X.obj.obj) → OpenSubspace X) (Z : ConnectedComponents (Point X.obj.obj) → AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (i : ∀ c, Z c ⟶ X) (hi : ∀ c, IsEtale (i c).hom.hom) (B : ConnectedComponents (Point X.obj.obj) → CommAlgCat.{u} k) (ρ : ∀ c, (Functor.const (Z c).EtaleSiteᵒᵖ).obj (CommRingCat.of (B c)) ⟶ (Z c).etaleForget.op ⋙ Scheme.Γ), (∀ c, Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk (CommRingCat.of (B c)) (ρ c)))) ∧ (∀ c, ∃ j : (Z c).obj.obj ≅ (U c).val.toFunctor, j.hom ≫ (U c).val.ι = (i c).hom.hom ∧ pointImage (U c).val.ι = ConnectedComponents.mk ⁻¹' {c}) ∧ (∀ c, Nontrivial (B c) ∧ IsLocalRing (B c) ∧ IsArtinianRing (B c) ∧ Module.Finite k (B c)) ∧ ∃ e : A ≃ₐ[k] (∀ c, B c), (∀ (a : A) (c : ConnectedComponents (Point X.obj.obj)) (T : (Z c).EtaleSite), ((ρ c).app (op T)).hom (e a c) = (π.app (op ((etaleMap (i c) (hi c)).obj T))).hom a) ∧ ((∀ T : X.EtaleSite, AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced (X.etaleForget.obj T)) → (∀ c, IsField (B c)) ∧ (IsAlgClosed k → (∃ constants : (ConnectedComponents (Point X.obj.obj) → k) ≃ₐ[k] A, ∀ (a : ConnectedComponents (Point X.obj.obj) → k) (c : ConnectedComponents (Point X.obj.obj)), e (constants a) c = algebraMap k (B c) (a c)) ∧ Module.finrank k A = Nat.card (ConnectedComponents (Point X.obj.obj))))
lean.note: The global algebras are specified by their limit cones on all small etale chart rings, with the scalar map normalized by the base map to Spec k. The factor algebras have the same limit-cone specification, and the product equivalence is characterized as restriction on every chart. Mathlib ConnectedComponents indexes precisely the maximal nonempty connected subsets. The empty point space is included, with a subsingleton global ring and an empty product. No definitions, assumptions of geometric reducedness, or statement corrections are introduced.
